Read event_rows and the mention/silver join, explored the 8 served events' headlines (read-only S3 GET), built _event_stories/_story_lead, tried threshold 2 (AC1(c) FAILED), moved to 1 with the ubiquitous-token drop (AC1 PASS). No S3 write, no vendor call, no deploy, no event split. One surprise row filed. STORY-GROUPING MECHANISM (publication_gold._event_stories): headline-token overlap over fields the rows already carry (the silver `title` join build_event supplies). A headline becomes a set of content tokens (lowercase ASCII alphanumerics, length>=3, small stopword list, one trailing plural 's' stripped). Tokens present in EVERY tier-A headline of the event (the security's own name, the day's topic) are dropped, since they cannot say which story a headline is in. Tier-A articles sharing at least ONE remaining token are joined (single-link connected components); a tier-B article never links two stories, it joins the story it overlaps most or stands alone. Lead = first article by the existing _event_sort_key of the story with the most tier-A articles; ties go to the story whose first article sorts earliest; a one-story event leads as before. FAILURE MODES: (1) MERGES wrongly when two different stories share one distinctive non-ubiquitous word (a generic word such as 'revenue' or 'record' in a 3+-tier-A event), which can hand the plurality to a false story; the ubiquitous-token drop does not catch it because the word is not in every headline. (2) SPLITS wrongly when one story's headlines share no surface token (paraphrase: 'jumps' vs 'surges'), so the story is undercounted and a real plurality can be missed. (3) The ubiquitous-token drop can remove a genuine story word ('jet' in the 2026-09-08 event) that is in all tier-A headlines; that costs nothing to the lead, since a token in every headline cannot separate stories, but an all-one-story event can print as split (the lead is the same either way). (4) In an event of exactly 2 tier-A articles no grouping can change the lead (1-1 tie or 2-0, first either way), so the mechanism is decisive only from 3 tier-A. (5) Non-ASCII characters (a corrupted apostrophe) are separators, so an accented word splits into fragments. Threshold history: 2 shared tokens was tried first and FAILED AC1(c) (the two deliveries headlines share only 'august' once 'jet' is ubiquitous); moved to 1.
